steps.text: Heat oil in a medium skillet. Add onion; cook until lightly browned. Stir in salt, cayenne pepper, turmeric and cumin.
Add potatoes; cook 10 minutes, stirring occasionally. Add tomatoes, cover pan, and cook until potatoes are soft, about 10 minutes more.

raw_recipe.headline: Aloo Phujia
raw_recipe.description: Aloo phujia is a spicy potatoes, tomatoes and onions dish with an Indian kick. This recipe includes cayenne pepper, ground turmeric, and ground cumin.
raw_recipe.name: Aloo Phujia

recipeInstructions.text: Heat oil in a medium skillet. Add onion; cook until lightly browned. Stir in salt, cayenne pepper, turmeric and cumin.
Add potatoes; cook 10 minutes, stirring occasionally. Add tomatoes, cover pan, and cook until potatoes are soft, about 10 minutes more.

review.reviewBody: I've been making Aloo Phujhi for years and everyone loves it. I always add some cut up sweet peppers, carrots and little broccoli. It gives it nice color. That's how they serve it at my favorite Indian restaurant. My family likes spicy so I kick the spice up quite a bit. I made this once for a party and the owner of a Indian restaurant was there and asked who made it and complimented me on how good it was. This recipe is a keeper!

I loved it. I choped the tomatoes, spices, half of the onion and some ginger in a food processor beforehand. 
Also boiled the potatoes for a few minutes already cubed. 

Than added the oil, onion and after 2-3min the potatoes. Adding the sauce from the processor and let it all boil for a while. So the spices come all out

I served it with some joghurt dip, for thise who don't eat to spicy. 

Will make it again :)

Delicious! Tripled the spices (turmeric and cumin), doubled the salt and cayenne pepper. Garnish with cilantro for a little extra something.

I cooked the potatoes for about 15 minutes before adding tomatoes, and it turned out perfectly. If they're not quite soft enough for you still, turn the stove on simmer, and leave the pan covered for another 5 minutes.

I cooked it but it was missing that extra kick or punch, so I added fresh cilantro and 1 serrano pepper cut into 5 pieces and I covered the pot for an extra 5 mins and served at with rice and a slice of fresh lime.

This recipe took me back to my days in Pakistan!!!

Thank you for sharing and keeping many memories alive...

Rabhyia

Easy recipe, explained well so you cannot go wrong. I found I had to add some water every once in a while to keep the dish from burning, but I used a cast iron pan, so it might be different in different pans. Great yellow colour! One note: It tastes well if you follow the recipe exactly, but to our taste it was a bit bland. So second time I added some mustard seeds and more cumin seeds, and the third time nigella seeds as well. This made it altogether spicier, which my family liked. Though I must say they finished the entire pan quickly every time I've cooked this! Will add cauliflower next time as well to make it more as Aloo Gobi.

39 3 15 ... http://allrecipes.com/recipe/14035/aloo-phujia/ ... Yup, I liked these potatoes. 'Even followed he directions except didn't add tomatoes. Spicy enough to last through a bite, but not lingering too long. Potatoes were half inch cubes & they were done according to directions. :) Oh, I added a cup, & then some, green peas to pretty it up.... Later: This is the same recipe as Food.com, but theirs reads 20 & 20. Similar offerings look good, too: http://www.food.com/recipe/aloo-phujia-61114 .... After cooking, I tossed in a quarter cup freshly chopped cilantro. 'Faked creme fraiche by combining sour cream & plain yogurt. Nice! :D

These were really quite good. I cooked the onions in butter, to add some flavor, and increased the spices, including salt, just a little. Also sprinkled red pepper flakes on top and pre-boiled the potatoes. I would suggest using a non-stick pan.

Very good but i tweaked it to my own preference, if you aren't a fan of greasy brown potatoes then try this: use only a little olive oil for the onion then as you're cooking and stirring add a smidge of vegetable broth whenever the potatoes start to stick a little, it'll cook away easily so it won't be soupy but will have a fresh clean taste.

First, I cooked the onions and added the spices. Then I added the potatoes. After letting the potatoes cooked for awhile, then I added the canned tomatoes with garlic and onions. It came out perfect. I microwave some Uncle Ben’s basmati rice and added it to the potatoes mixture. Wasn’t too spicy for me.

I used rose potatoes so I didn't peel. I par baked in microwave while spices cooked. I halved the salt and cayenne, too spicy for my dad. After cooking I added a little of seasoned salt and pepper. And crushed reds to my portion to add the heat back.

Like some other reviewers, I found the original recipe to be too bland, so I tripled the spices (except the salt) and added some coriander. I also softened the potatoes ahead of time in the microwave and included some green peppers for good measure.
This is a family favourite! We add capsicum, carrot, and broccoli and serve with a dollop of plain yoghurt. Totally delicious 😋
Read through other reviews. I doubled the spices and added 1/2 tsp each of chili powder and ground coriander. Delicious!
Love these potatoes. Very good as leftovers too. Made it with Indian Tomato Chicken and they were delish together.

Absolutely delicious. The flavors all came together wonderfully. It didnt seem like it would but it did. I would half the cayenne and then add more if you want more kick. Otherwise, your stuck if you add the full amount. I went with half the amount and it was perfect hear. I also threw in some brocolli and gave it a little bit more dimension and color. Very tasty.

This is my first experience of Indian food, and also in making something vegetarian. I thought it was going to be pretty good, but since I had never used turmeric before, I wasn't exactly sure what to fully expect in terms of flavor. I saw that all of the ingredients were things my family already has, and today I decided I'd make it for my lunch.

It smelled absolutely delicious as it was cooking, and I wasn't sure exactly how adding the tomatoes and covering to finish cooking for 10 minutes was going to work, because there was no added liquid like I'm used to when doing that, and wasn't sure if I would need to stir at all. I had hoped that the tomatoes would provide enough juices that the potatoes wouldn't stick to the bottom and burn. Happily enough, as soon as I added the tomatoes that was exactly what happened, and I realized that stirring probably wouldn't be needed after covering.

In terms of flavor, it's a knock out. I so want to eat the other three servings, the potatoes are just so good. The tomatoes themselves didn't take up too much of the seasoning, mainly just tasting like ordinary cooked tomatoes, but that's not to say they are bad. It's just something someone who dislikes cooked tomatoes would probably pick out. I personally like cooked tomato, I just know someone who doesn't.
Aloo Phujia by Christyj. Half inch cubed potatoes, no tomatoes, added peas & fresh cilantro; faked creme fraiche with sour cream & plain yogurt.
I made it just as written and it was excellent.
Will definitely make again!
I will definitely have to make this dish again, it was delicious and a good dish to make for any dinner or time.
